findings.title: Unguarded update in catch block can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The new retry increment in the catch block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If the Prisma update fails (DB blip, connection issue, or the reminder was deleted concurrently, which makes update throw P2025), the exception escapes the for-loop and the handler. Every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped for this run, and the request fails. One bad reminder should not block the others. Wrap the update, or use updateMany, which does not throw on zero matches.

findings.title: Retry counter is a read-modify-write on a stale value
findings.body: The count is computed as `reminder.retryCount + 1` from the value read at the start of the run (lines 184 and 195). If two cron invocations overlap, or the value changed since the findMany, increments are lost and the reminder can keep retrying past the intended limit. Use an atomic update such as `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`.

findings.title: retryCount deletion clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The OR branch `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` has no `method` filter, so it deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method, and regardless of whether it is scheduled. The SMS-only intent of this job is lost. Today only the SMS path increments retryCount, so this is latent, but any future increment elsewhere would delete unrelated email or WhatsApp reminders. Scope the condition to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and `scheduled: false`.

findings.title: Unindexed retryCount filter runs on every cron invocation
findings.body: The new `retryCount > 1` predicate runs inside deleteMany on every cron tick. The migration adds no index on retryCount, and the existing WorkflowReminder indexes do not cover it, so this OR branch forces a scan of the WorkflowReminder table on each run. Consider an index or a narrower predicate.

findings.title: Reminders with no message are retried forever and never counted
findings.body: Retry counting only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` (the else branch at line 178) and in the catch. If the message is empty or sendTo is missing, neither path increments retryCount, so the reminder stays unscheduled and is reconsidered on every run indefinitely. This is the same unbounded retry the PR is meant to stop. Such reminders should also count as failures or be removed.

findings.title: Retry limit semantics are not documented and the threshold is off-by-one in appearance
findings.body: The code deletes when retryCount > 1, so a reminder gets two failed attempts before deletion. The PR description says 'after scheduling failed twice we delete', which matches, but the `gt: 1` threshold reads like 'delete on the second failure' to a maintainer. Neither the code nor the description makes the limit a named constant, so the intent is easy to get wrong when changed.

findings.title: No tests for the retry and deletion behavior
findings.body: The PR changes cron behavior (retry increment on failure, deletion after the limit, the new catch-path update) but adds no tests. Nothing verifies that a failed Twilio schedule increments the counter, that a reminder is deleted after the limit, or that a thrown error does not stop the loop.
